For a unit vector  

  n = (sin θ, 0, cos θ)   (lying in the x–z plane, azimuth φ = 0)

the operator whose eigenvector we want is  

  P·n = (ħ/2)(σ_x sin θ + σ_z cos θ).

Using the Pauli matrices  

  σ_x = [[0,1],[1,0]],  σ_z = [[1,0],[0,-1]],

we have  

  σ_x sin θ + σ_z cos θ = [[cos θ, sin θ],[sin θ, -cos θ]].

Let v = (a, b)^T be an eigenvector with eigenvalue +1 of this (ħ/2 factor removed):

  [[cos θ, sin θ],[sin θ, -cos θ]] (a,b)^T = (a,b)^T.

This gives the simultaneous equations  

1) (cos θ − 1)a + sin θ b = 0  
2) sin θ a − (cos θ + 1)b = 0.

From (1):

  b/a = (1 − cos θ)/sin θ = tan(θ/2).

Thus v is proportional to (1, tan (θ/2)).  
Choosing the normalization constant a = cos (θ/2),

  v_norm = (cos (θ/2), sin (θ/2)),

and |v_norm|² = cos²(θ/2) + sin²(θ/2) = 1, so it is already normalized.

Hence the normalized eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue +ħ/2 is  

  (cos (θ/2), sin (θ/2)).

Among the given choices, this is option (B).

Answer: B
